title: Distributed Launching and Fault Tolerance knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “torchrun” in this lesson?
options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Document the rank/process topology, data partitioning, collective operations, and checkpoint ownership, then test the smallest supported launch.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
questions.answer_key: Document the rank/process topology, data partitioning, collective operations, and checkpoint ownership, then test the smallest supported launch.
questions.explanation: torchrun: Document the rank/process topology, data partitioning, collective operations, and checkpoint ownership, then test the smallest supported launch.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Process configuration”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
ensure each rank is initialized correctly, data sampling is distributed, collectives match across ranks, and cleanup handles failures.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: ensure each rank is initialized correctly, data sampling is distributed, collectives match across ranks, and cleanup handles failures.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: ensure each rank is initialized correctly, data sampling is distributed, collectives match across ranks, and cleanup handles failures.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Worker failures”?
options: Do not run a DDP script as an ordinary single Python process without its required distributed initialization.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Do not run a DDP script as an ordinary single Python process without its required distributed initialization.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not run a DDP script as an ordinary single Python process without its required distributed initialization.
